conviction_note: Two forces roughly cancel. On one side the quarter's revenue looks set to beat: two pipeline fills (Rhode Sephora Europe, e.l.f. Hair at Target) plus an easy year-ago core comp. The full-year guide also implies only about +5-8% H2 growth, which leaves room to raise. On the other side the stock goes in at its 52-week closing high, up about 26% since the last print, after a wave of October target raises, with a +27 vol-point put skew, a buy-side whisper about 20% above consensus, and a soft core makeup category. So p_up is 48 on a 12% abs move. The findings sum to about -0.1 and the scaled number is -0.48; both are effectively zero, and they agree on a weak downside lean.
bar: Q2 FY27 revenue $470.6m (+36.8% y/y) and adjusted EPS $0.61. Two estimate sources agree: the Zacks preview (https://tradingview.com/news/zacks:953834406094b:0-e-l-f-beauty-readies-for-q2-earnings-what-should-investors-expect) and Earnings Whispers via Finviz, 2026-10-27 (https://finviz.com/news/409483/elf-beauty-faces-proof-test-as-rodes-european-launch-meets-a-soft-core-brand), which also gives a $0.73 whisper. The company guided 'mid-30s' total sales growth for Q2, about $461-468m on the $343.9m year-ago base, so consensus sits at or slightly above the top of the guide. FY27 guide (2026-08-05): net sales $1,938-1,968m, adjusted EBITDA $401-407m, adjusted EPS $3.50-3.55 (https://investor.elfbeauty.com/stock-and-financial/press-releases/landing-news/2026/08-05-2026-210618204). Year-ago Q2 FY26: revenue $343.9m, adjusted EPS $0.68.
positioning_check: Short interest 4.11M shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, 3.1 days to cover (massive.com quote page dated 2026-10-23, https://massive.com/quote/elf). That is about 7% of roughly 59.0M shares outstanding: not crowded. Baseline: 25-delta skew +26.97 vol points (puts bid hard), put/call OI 0.27 (call-heavy open interest), event-implied move 11.62%, spot 117.60, 0.6% off the 52-week closing high, +11.96% over 20 days. October brought a cluster of target raises: Baird 105->120 (10-07), Citi 118->130 (10-14), Morgan Stanley 90->103 and UBS neutral $116 (10-15), Jefferies 100->132 (10-19), Canaccord 123->137 (10-22), Zacks Rank #1, Wall Street Zen upgrade (10-31) (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/analyst-elf-beauty-nyse-elf-stock-gets-price-target-increase-from-jefferies-financial-group-2026-10-19/). The sell-side bar has ratcheted up into the print, and the option market is paying for downside.

findings.finding: Q2 (Jul-Sep 2026) revenue carries two one-time pipeline fills: Rhode's Sephora launch in 19 European countries and about 500 stores on 2026-09-30, sell-in inside the quarter, and e.l.f. Hair going into all US Target stores on 2026-07-05. It also laps a depressed year-ago core: Q2 FY26 ex-Rhode sales fell 3% because e.l.f. halted shipments to some retailers. Against a 'mid-30s' guide (~$461-468m) and a $470.6m consensus, a print near $480m (+2% vs bar) is plausible. e.l.f. beat Q1 revenue by about $48m (11%). Management explicitly attributed the mid-30s guide partly to the Rhode Europe pipeline, though, so much of this sits inside the guide, and previews already flag that sell-in is not sell-through.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY27 (2026-08-05): revenue beat by about 11% with a guide raise, +6.88%. Q4 FY26 (2026-05-20): revenue beat, +4.73% close-to-close, though early gains were wiped intraday on core softness. Q2 FY26 (2025-11-05): revenue missed $365.8m consensus at $343.9m with a weak guide, -35.04%. Revenue surprises have moved this stock, but the guide dominated the large moves.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. Consensus at 36.8% already sits at the top of the mid-30s guide, and the stock is up about 26% since the Q1 print. If the market expected a large beat, consensus would have drifted above the guide in the last 30 days; Zacks says it moved only one penny on EPS, with ESP -1.64%. What is not in consensus is the easy year-ago core comp from the shipment halt, which previews do not mention.
findings.independence: Year-ago halted shipments, ex-Rhode -3%: https://www.tipranks.com/news/e-l-f-beauty-stock-elf-plunges-as-intl-sales-slow-outlook-disappoints-wall-street (2025-11-06). Target Hair all-store date 2026-07-05: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260615770928/en/. Sell-in caveat and BofA's $150-200m annual Rhode Europe sizing: https://www.thestreet.com/investing/elf-beauty-rhode-sephora-europe-bofa-stock-price-target (403 on fetch; seen as a search snippet only).

findings.finding: The FY27 guide of $1,938-1,968m, less Q1's reported $479.4m and Q2 at the $470.6m consensus, implies H2 net sales of about $988-1,018m. The FY26 base is about $1,641m (from the guide's 18-20% growth); with H1 FY26 at $697.6m, H2 FY26 was about $943m, so the implied H2 FY27 growth is only about +5-8%. Rhode Europe distribution is new in H2, and BofA sizes it at $150-200m a year (about $75-100m a half, or 8-10 points of H2 growth on its own). The remaining-three-quarter adjusted EPS implied by the guide is also only about $1.75-1.80 after Q1's refund-inflated $1.75. Read literally, the guide implies a declining core, or it is conservative and leaves room for a raise on this print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance has decided every large move. 2026-08-05: FY raise from 12-14% to 18-20% growth, +6.88% (+18.8% over the week per Zacks). 2025-11-05: FY guide below Street, -35.04%. 2025-02-06: guide cut, -19.62%.
findings.why_not_priced: The arithmetic is public. But the October target raises and the 26% run since August suggest the Street already models a raise. If the market were pricing no raise, the stock would not sit at its 52-week closing high with targets at $130-137. So this is a raise the market half-expects. The finding's value is that the guide's own math leaves the room, not that nobody has noticed.
findings.independence: BofA's Rhode Europe sizing (TheStreet, snippet only). Earnings Whispers preview notes the full-year guide implies 10-12% organic growth for the remaining quarters, which says the same thing from another angle: https://finviz.com/news/409483/elf-beauty-faces-proof-test-as-rodes-european-launch-meets-a-soft-core-brand. Both rest on the same company guide document.

findings.finding: The core e.l.f. brand and mass makeup category were soft going into and through the quarter. Q1 FY27 ex-Rhode sales fell high-single digits, with units about -3 points, and brand consumption had slowed to low single digits by May. Ulta's May-July quarter showed mass makeup down low-single digits (2026-08-27). Estée Lauder's Jul-Sep makeup grew only +1% organic (2026-11-02). Circana's H1 2026 mass makeup was +5% on falling units. In Q2 e.l.f. starts lapping its August 2025 $1 price increase while cutting prices on some families. Organic quality and the core-brand commentary are therefore at risk even if Rhode carries the total.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-05-20: revenue beat, but core-brand softness and the Morgan Stanley 'disconcerting' share comment wiped the early gains, and the stock closed only +4.73%. 2025-11-05: the ex-Rhode decline was part of a -35% day.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly public, and the previews call the core brand 'the weaker link'. The Estée Lauder makeup print of 2026-11-02 landed after e.l.f. last spoke. If the softness were fully priced, sell-side targets would not have moved up 15-30% in October. This is a proxy: no direct e.l.f. Q2 scanner figure was found, and Rhode, about a third of sales, is net of it.
findings.independence: Estée Lauder 8-K, makeup +1% organic: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001001250/000100125026000057/fy2027q1exhibit991.htm (2026-11-02). Circana H1 2026: https://www.premiumbeautynews.com/en/us-beauty-market-stays-strong-in,28150. Q1 ex-Rhode decline: https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/2974358/elf-jumps-188-in-a-week-amid-rhode-growth-and-stronger-guidance. Offsetting context: Estée Lauder raised its FY27 outlook and L'Oréal North America grew +5.6% adjusted in Q3, so the overall beauty category is healthy and makeup is the soft part.

findings.finding: Q2 EPS setup. Consensus is $0.61 against a $0.73 whisper and $0.68 a year ago. Q1 marketing came in at 22% of sales, below plan 'because of spending timing', and accrued marketing fell from $43.3m to $16.0m, so spend moves into Q2 and H2. Q2 also carries price cuts funded by the refund, and no further IEEPA refund is recorded as receivable (about $9m of the $60.3m paid is unrecovered). e.l.f. has beaten EPS by an average 61.5% over four quarters, so a beat is expected and the whisper is 20% above consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS beats have not reliably paid. 2026-05-20: EPS beat +70%, then the stock sold off intraday before closing +4.73%. 2026-02-04: EPS beat, -9.18%. 2025-11-05: EPS beat ($0.68 vs $0.57), -35%.
findings.why_not_priced: The whisper is already 20% above consensus, so an ordinary beat is in the price. The marketing phasing in the 10-Q is the part that is less visible: it could make Q2 EPS land below the whisper even if it clears consensus.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers whisper $0.73: https://finviz.com/news/409483/elf-beauty-faces-proof-test-as-rodes-european-launch-meets-a-soft-core-brand. Zacks surprise history and ESP: https://tradingview.com/news/zacks:953834406094b:0-e-l-f-beauty-readies-for-q2-earnings-what-should-investors-expect.

findings.finding: The Rhode earnout measurement period ends 2026-09-30, and contingent consideration was already raised to $80.8m (maximum $200m) because Rhode beat its thresholds: a $57.6m charge in Q4 FY26 and $16.1m in Q1 FY27. A further GAAP fair-value charge in Q2 is likely and is excluded from adjusted EPS. It is a GAAP-only one-off, and it also reads as confirmation that Rhode is still beating plan.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q1 FY27 $16.1m charge was reported alongside the +6.88% day; it was not the driver.
findings.why_not_priced: It is below operating income and excluded from the adjusted numbers the Street trades on, so it is near zero either way. Its only path to the multiple is as a Rhode-strength signal.
findings.independence: Same 10-Q as the EPS-setup finding and the capital-return finding; the three facts are distinct.

findings.finding: Expectations have ratcheted up into the print. The stock is +26% since the Q1 report and +12% over 20 days, sits 0.6% off its 52-week closing high, and rose from $111.69 (10-30) to $117.60. October brought six target raises to $103-137. The whisper is 20% above consensus. The option market prices an 11.6% move with a +27 vol-point put skew. Short interest of about 7% and 3.1 days to cover is not crowded enough to make a squeeze a mechanism.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Of the last six prints, the stock rose only after the two that came off depressed bases (2026-05 and 2026-08). The four that came into higher expectations (2025-02, 2025-08, 2025-11, 2026-02) fell 9-35%.
findings.why_not_priced: This agrees with the skew, so the option market is already paying for it. It is filed because the bar the print must clear has moved up since the consensus was set, which consensus EPS and revenue do not show.
findings.independence: Baseline skew and run-up (sealed file). Earnings Whispers: sentiment moved from 'deeply bearish to mildly bearish', with shares far above the 200-day: https://finviz.com/news/409483/elf-beauty-faces-proof-test-as-rodes-european-launch-meets-a-soft-core-brand. findings.finding: Routine insider selling in Sept-Oct 2026, all under 10b5-1 plans. On 2026-10-01 CEO Tarang Amin exercised 71,000 options and sold 47,000 shares at $102.29-105.37 to cover withholding. Smaller executive sales followed on 10-14 and 10-19. Over three months insiders sold 96,068 shares, about $9.8m.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed reaction to these sales.
findings.why_not_priced: Public and plan-driven, so it carries essentially no information.

findings.finding: $350m remains under the 2024 buyback authorization, and e.l.f. bought $50m (900,063 shares at $55.53) in Q1. Cash was $344.2m against $834.2m of debt at 2026-06-30. Any buyback update or added repurchase is a small positive; at $117 the stock is double the Q1 buyback price, which makes aggressive buying less likely.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q1 buyback was disclosed with the +6.88% print; not separable.
findings.why_not_priced: It is small relative to a $6.8bn market cap, and the authorization is public.
findings.independence: Same 10-Q as the EPS-setup and earnout findings.

findings.finding: Tariff regime change inside the quarter: on 2026-07-24 Section 301 tariffs of 10-12.5% on 60 economies replaced the Section 122 10% duty. On China-sourced product (25% base since 2019), that puts the rate around the 35% the FY27 outlook assumes, or slightly above it, at up to about 37.5%. It is a marginal gross-margin headwind from late July and is mostly an H2 item.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Tariff headlines drove the 2025-08 (-9.48%) and 2025-11 (-35%) prints when rates were around 55%. At about 35% this is a much smaller line.
findings.why_not_priced: Disclosed in the 10-Q and roughly in line with the outlook's assumed rate, so it is near zero.
findings.independence: The 35% outlook assumption, as summarised from the FY26 10-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001600033/000160003326000020/elf-20260331.htm.

baseline_tension: Mixed. The positioning finding and the soft-core proxy agree with the +27 put skew and the stretched run-up, while the revenue-setup and guide-room findings cut against it. The net lean is slightly negative and small, so p_up stays near 50.
lessons_applied: Revenue-setup finding (reported_quarter) cut from +1.0 to +0.6: it lands largely inside the company's 'mid-30s' guide, which management tied to the Rhode Europe pipeline (lessons 1 and 6)
Guide-room finding cut from +1.5 to +1.2: it runs against a strong put skew, and there is no document-level reason the option market is wrong (lesson 7)
Core-makeup softness cut from -1.5 to -1.0: it rests on peer and category proxies, not an e.l.f. number, and Rhode (about a third of sales) is net of it (lessons 5 and 9)
Positioning finding cut from -2.0 to -1.5: it agrees with the skew, so it is largely already priced
abs_move_pct and p_up left at 12.0 and 48: the lessons move findings toward 0 and p_up toward 50, and p_up was already there
